Respectfully submitted,
Erik Gulbranson
May 13, 2026

By:	/s/ Erik Gulbranson     		May 13, 2026

19901 Firefly Road
Florence, Texas 76527
Telephone: 512-639-3888
Email: rollingoaksglass@yahoo.com

INTRODUCTION 
Q. PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME FOR THE RECORD. 
	A. Erik Gulbranson
Q. PLEASE STATE YOUR ADDRESS FOR THE RECORD. 
	A. 19901 Firefly Road, Florence Texas 76527
Q. DO ANY OF THE PROPOSED TRANSMISSION ROUTES IMPACT PROPERTY YOU OWN? 
	A. Yes
Q. LIST THE SPECIFIC ROUTE LINK(S) THAT IMPACT PROPERTY YOU OWN?
	A. G71, G72, and G73

NOTICE AND PUBLIC MEETINGS
Q. DID YOU RECEIVE A NOTICE IN THE MAIL FROM THE APPLICANTS LAST SPRING ABOUT THE PROJECT AND THE JUNE 2025 PUBLIC MEETINGS?
	A. No
Q. DID YOU RECEIVE A PACKET IN THE MAIL FROM THE APPLICANTS REGARDING THE PROPOSED TRANSMISSION LINE ROUTES?
	A. Yes
Q. WHEN DID YOU RECEIVE THAT PACKET IN THE MAIL?
	A. I received the packet from Oncor in the mail on March 30, 2026.
Q. DID YOU RECEIVE ANY NOTIFICATION FROM THE APPLICANTS OR THE PUC ABOUT THE PROJECT PRIOR TO RECENT PACKET YOU RECEIVED IN THE MAIL IN MARCH 2026?
	A. No, I did not.
Q. DO YOU KNOW WHY YOU DID NOT RECEIVE A NOTICE ABOUT THE JUNE 2025 PUBLIC MEETINGS?
A. I believe I was not notified because the route links that impact my property were added sometime after the public meeting was held.

ATTEMPTS TO OBTAIN LEGAL REPRESENTATION  
Q. ONCE YOU RECEIVED YOUR NOTIFICATION, DID YOU ATTEMPT TO OBTAIN LEGAL REPRESENTATION?
	A. Yes

Q. APPROXIMATELY HOW MANY LAW OFFICES THAT SPECIALIZE IN PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF TEXAS LEGAL PROCEEDINGS DID YOU CONTACT IN AN ATTEMPT TO OBTAIN LEGAL REPRESENTATION?
A. My wife contacted approximately ten law offices and/or legal professionals that specialize in Public Utility Commission proceedings on my behalf.

Q. OF THE SPECIALIZED LAW OFFICES YOU CONTACTED, HOW MANY WERE AVAILABLE TO TAKE YOU AS A CLIENT?
A. Of those that responded to us, none were available. We were told that they were already representing other landowners, and that it would be a conflict of interest for them to represent us. The other landowners had the opportunity to hire legal representation soon after the June 2025 meeting.
Q. IF A LAW OFFICE WITH SPECIALIZED EXPERTISE WOULD HAVE BEEN AVAILABLE TO ACCEPT YOU AS A CLIENT, WOULD YOU HAVE MOVED FORWARD WITH LEGAL REPRESENTATION?
A. Yes, if specialized representation had been available, I would have retained them myself, or coordinated with neighbors to retain them as a group.

DUE PROCESS AND TIMELINE CONCERNS
Q. HAS THE CONSTRAINED TIMELINE RESULTING FROM ONCOR’S AND LCRA’S FAILURE TO NOTIFY YOU, AND AS IMPOSED BY THE SHORT 180-DAY TIMEFRAME FOR THESE PROCEEDINGS, COMBINED WITH THE LACK OF AVAILABLE LEGAL REPRESENTATION, HAMPERED YOUR ABILITY TO EFFECTIVELY NAVIGATE THE PROJECT AND LEGAL PROCEDURES AS IS NECESSARY TO EXERCISE YOUR RIGHTS OF DUE PROCESS?
A. Yes. In my opinion, this process has created a major disadvantage for ordinary landowners and has hindered any meaningful participation and due process protections that should be offered equally to all in proceedings of this scope and consequence.

The shortened timeline and inability to secure legal represention has greatly hindered my
ability to properly and adequatly understand, prepare for and participate in these proceedings.

The procedural requirements that are associated with Public Utility Commission proceedings are technical and very unfamiliar to ordinary landowners like myself. Unlike the Applicants, the Commission Staff, and parties who participate in these proceedings routinely as part of their profession, us affected landowners are having to defend our homes, our property rights, our family interests and responsibilities while simultaneously running a business, maintaining family obligations and responsibilities. 

This shortened procedural schedule has severely limited my ability to sufficiantly review filings, understand requirements, prepare testimony, evalute other proposed route alternatives, and meaningfully participate in this process. This situation was only further worsened because many qualified attorneys familiar with Public Utility Commission litigation had already been retained by others involved in the proceedings, which made legal representation unavailable to many of us landowners.

Q. CURRENTLY, WHAT ARE YOUR BIGGEST STRUGGLES REGARDING THE PROJECT?
A. According to the packet we received in the mail from Oncor the "link composition for alternative filed routes in the CCN application: Bell County East Switch - Big Hill Substation 765-kV Transmission Line Project" includes 122 potential routes.

Link G71 ends in the southeast corner of our neighbor, Mr. Vanderboom's property. This is on the northeast corner fence line of our property. Out of Oncor’s 122 potential routes, G71 is included in 66 of the routes. G71 is included in approximately 54% of the routes.

Link G72 goes across our back pasture and runs along our fence line from the southeast corner of our property to the northeast corner. Out of Oncor's 122 potential routes, G72 is included in 26 of the routes. Out of the 122 potential routes, G72 is included in approximately 21% of the routes. A 200' wide easement crossing 1121.22' of our pasture would be a total of 224,244 square feet, which equals 5.14 acres of our pasture. In addition to the acreage in this easement, there will be much more adjacent acreage that in my opinion will not be available to us for future land use and improvements.

Although Link G73 would run east to west through our neighbor's property, it would be the most damaging to our family, our home, our established small business, and our livestock operation. G73 would be north of our property, but within approximately 300' to 400' of our home and my shop in my estimations based on the available Oncor interactive map found online. Out of the 122 potential routes, G73 is included in 92 of the routes. Out of Oncor’s 122 potential routes, G73 is included in approximately 75% of the routes. G73 would run between where our livestock barn and nightly holding pen is located and our neighbor’s (Mr. Hoffman) home which are approximately 679.57' apart. G73 would also run between our home and shop are located and Mr. Vanderboom's home, which are approximately 850.68' apart. By my estimations, this would put our home, shop, and barn all well within 500’ of the proposed G73 transmission line. 

Overall, out of Oncor’s 122 potential routes, at least one of these three links (G71, G72, and G73) is included in 92 of them, which is 75% of the potential routes. 75% of Oncor's potential paths would greatly affect my family, my business, my future land use, and our ranch. I personally do not feel that this project and these potential routes show a fair amount of geographic diversity.
Our home, our shop, and both of our adjacent neighbor's homes (Vanderboom and Hoffman) are not currently showing on Oncor's interactive map due to the current map being, what I believe to be, nearly 4 years old. Our home, our shop, our barn, and the Vanderboom home are however shown on current Google satellite maps. This causes me to question why Oncor chooses to use dated and inaccurate arial maps when planning land paths for a project of this size and expense. In my estimation, the current (as of 5/13/2026) interactive map that Oncor provides on their website uses satellite imagery that was taken between the dates of July 5, 2022 and July 14, 2022. I am basing my timeline for the Oncor interactive map date on my personal photographs of our home and shop build that was underway during the timeframe listed.

Q. WHAT IS THE WORST PART ABOUT THE CURRENT SITUATION?
A. For me the worst part is that this process is moving way too fast for such a massive project. We were offered no PUC public meeting or workshop to help educate us about the process. I have not had the time to adequately get prepared. I have not had the time neccessary to learn how to properly defend my rights. I have not had the opportunity to find an experienced attorney that is not already retained by other landowners who were given more time. With such a short time frame landowners like myself are lost and trying to quickly catch up to learn what to do and how to do it.

Q. ARE YOUR NEIGHBORS IN A SIMILAR SITUATION?
A. Yes. Unfortunately, my neighbors are also lost in this process. Many are elderly and did not even understand what these 765-kV transmission lines are or how to participate in this process. There were landowners contacted prior to the June meeting who were given a ten month headstart on myself and my neighbors. We are now at a huge disadvantage because Oncor and LCRA chose to not notify us at the same time as other landowners that their preferred links are proposed to come right through these properties. They did however choose to notify other landowners in advance, but did not notify myself or my neighbors even though 75% of their proposed routes would go through or beside our land.

Q. WHAT COULD HAVE OR SHOULD HAVE BEEN DONE DIFFERENTLY, IN YOUR OPINION?
A. Oncor and LCRA should have informed us when they added our routes. They should have given us a full meeting like the one offered in June. I was not allowed the opportunity to ask questions, give comment, or express concerns. I was thrown into a process already quickly moving forward. The PUC knew they were adding routes, and they should been required to notify us in advance. I feel this whole system is rigged for landowners like myself, and can‘t help but feel that we were intentionally notified at the last minute.

Q. IN YOUR OPINION, WHAT SHOULD BE DONE TO REPAIR THE DAMAGE DONE TO YOU BY NOT BEING NOTIFIED WHEN YOUR ROUTE WAS FIRST CONSIDERED, AS WAS DONE WITH THE ROUTE SHOWN AT THE JUNE 2025 HEARING?
A. There are so many people who have been blindsided and denied the due process that many others were granted. Oncor and LCRA should have held addtional public meetings. Or they should have postponed the one they held until they were ready to include all landowners affected by these proposed routes.

Simply put, I need more time. I need time to give comments. Oncor and LCRA need time to review and incorporate those comments, just like they did with all who were properly notified back in June of 2025. I need time to provide Oncor and LCRA information about structures and buildings and important things on our property, and they need time to incorporate those into the study. Time is what has been taken from us by Oncor and LCRA and time is what I need. The opportunities I have been denied so far, due to Oncor and LCRA not informing when they should have, greatly impact the future for my family and our property. Oncor and LCRA started a marathon, but did not let us begin the race until everyone else was already nearing the finish line. 

Q. IN YOUR OPINION, IS THERE ANYTHING THAT CAN BE DONE NOW TO REMEDY YOUR LOSS OF DUE PROCESS?
A. Yes, there is. Myself, my family, and all of the people on route links that were added
 
after the public meeting held in June who were not notified (even though Oncor and 

LCRA knew that we were directly impacted) should all be given the same consideration 

many others were offered. The PUC must determine how to fix this. I should be given an 

equal opportunity to properly prepare to participate in this process. They should restore 

my rights of due process.


Q. DO YOU HAVE ANYTHING ELSE YOU WOULD LIKE TO PROVIDE THAT IS IMPORTANT TO LET THE PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION KNOW ABOUT YOUR LAND, YOUR FAMILY, OR THESE PROCEEDINGS?

A. Through generational accounts of the land and specifically arranged rocks, we understand there to be five Native American burial sites located in the back portion of our property that potentially could be affected by the land clearing and equipment needed to construct link G72. Our property is approximately 2.5 miles from the extraordinary Gault archaeological dig site, so it should be understood that all of these surrounding areas had heavy Native American activity, and the artifacts that have been found on our land and in the surrounding areas provide strong evidence of that. I  feel very strongly that this information needs to be included in the public record, and that it is my duty as the land‘s current caregiver to do what I can to convey the importance of that area. This burial site deserves to be treated with the same respect one would give any cemetery. I would hope that anybody that ever works on this land, inherits this land, or purchases this land in the future would understand the need to tread lightly and respect this potentially sacred area the same way my family and I have done, and the same way families who cared for this land for generations before me have done. 
Other concerns that I have are as follows: noise from the lines and that noise being amplified inside of my metal shop building. The potential health effects of 765-kV for my four young growing children, my wife and myself, as I have not been able to find any U.S. based long term health studies on 765-kV lines. The possibility of having to relocate my established business, home, and livestock. The loss of value and potential use of my property. Our children not being able to build their future homes on our land. Limits on the use of large portions of our land in the future (we do not feel that we would be able to build or develop anywhere near those lines). 
Additionally, there are flood plains on part of the land that limit its use, and these lines are over or near some of the most useful parts of the land for building. I have worked hard for 32 years to get to the point where my wife and I could purchase land like this for our family, and it would be extremely difficult to replace this land and all the work we have invested in it while also staying local to our community and church family. I do not wish to start over and rebuild everything I have at this stage in my life.
As a husband and parent, my number one job and priority is to protect the health and safety of my wife and children. If these proposed transmission lines were to run near or through our land, I will be left with no choice but to relocate my business and family due to the lack of long-term studies on the the health impacts of 765-kV transmission lines in near proximity to habitable dwellings. I cannot and will not allow my family to become the long-term study.
Q.  DO YOU HAVE A FINAL REQUEST? 
A. Yes. I request that Oncor’s and LCRA’s request for CCN on the 59475 Bell County 

East to Big Hill 765-kV transmission line be denied for knowingly withholding notice and 

failure to properly notify hundreds of directly impacted landowners.


Q. DOES THIS CONCLUDE YOUR DIRECT TESTIMONY? 
	A. Yes.

LAND, YOUR FAMILY, OR THESE PROCEEDINGS?



      A. Through generational accounts of the land and specifically arranged rocks, we

      understand there to be five Native American burial sites located in the back portion of

      our property that potentially could be affected by the land clearing and equipment

      needed to construct link G72. Our property is approximately 2.5 miles from the

      extraordinary Gault archaeological dig site, so it should be understood that all Of these

      surrounding areas had heavy Native American activity, and the artifacts that have been

      found on our land and in the surrounding areas provide strong evidence ofthat. I feel

      very strongly that this information needs to be included in the public record, and that it is

      my duty as the land's current caregiver to do what I can to convey the importance of that

      area. This burial site deserves to be treated with the same respect one would give any

      cemetery. I would hope that anybody that ever works on this land, inherits this land, or

      purchases this land in the future would understand the need to tread lightly and respect

      this potentially sacred area the same way my family and I have done, and the same way

      families who cared for this land for generations before me have done.


      Other concerns that I have are as follows: noise from the lines and that noise being

      amplified inside ofmy metal shop building. The potential health effects of 765-kVfor my

      property. Our children not being able to build their future homes on our land. Limits on

      the use of large portions of our land in the future (we do not feel that we would be able to

      build or develop anywhere near those lines).


      Additionally, there are flood plains on part Of the land that limit its use, and these lines

      are over or near some Of the most useful parts Of the land for building. I have worked


      hard for 32 years to get to the point where my wife and I could purchase land like this for

      our family, and it would be extremely difficult to replace this land and all the work we

      have invested in it while also staying local to our community and church family. I do not

      wish to start over and rebuild everything I have at this stage in my life.

      As a husband and parent, my number one job and priority is to protect the health and

      safety ofmywife and children. If these proposed transmission lines were to run near or

      through our land, I will be left with no choice but to relocate my business and family due

      to the lack Of long-term studies on the the health impacts Of 765-kV transmission lines in


      near proximity to habitable dwellings. I cannot and will not allow my family to become

      the long-term study.


Q. DO YOU HAVE A FINAL REQUEST?

      A. Yes. I request that Oncor's and LCRA's request for CCN on the 59475 Bell County

      East to Big Hill 765-kV transmission line be denied for knowingly withholding notice and

      failure to properly notify hundreds of directly impacted landowners.
